title: perf/bench: add benchmark artifact uploader + structured metadata manifest
author: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Motivation: We’ve been seeing run-to-run variance and “can’t reproduce” benchmark deltas during the FP8/INT8 sprint. A big contributor is missing provenance: which runtime SHA, CUDA/driver pair, GPU clocks/power settings, model revision, and benchmark config were actually used for a run. This PR adds (1) a structured metadata manifest that is emitted with every benchmark artifact (microbench + e2e), and (2) an uploader that bundles results + metadata and pushes to our artifact store with stable naming.

What ships in this PR:
- New benchmark artifact schema: benchmark_metadata.json (v1)
  - git: repo, commit_sha, dirty_tree, branch (best-effort), build_id
  - runtime: version string, build type, feature flags (sanitized)
  - container: image_ref + digest, cuda_runtime_version, cudnn_version (if present)
  - driver/hardware: nvidia_driver_version, gpu_name, gpu_uuid (hashed), mig_mode, sm_count, gpu_mem_gb, pcie_gen (if available)
  - clocks/power: graphics_clock_mhz (locked/target), sm_clock_mhz, mem_clock_mhz, power_limit_w, persistence_mode
  - environment: region, cluster, instance_type, hostname (hashed), kernel_version
  - model: model_id, model_family, model_revision, model_hash (sha256 of weights index/manifest), quant_mode (fp16/bf16/fp8/int8), kv_cache_dtype
  - benchmark: suite_name (e.g. top-hosted-models-benchmark-suite-v3), workload_id, prompt_dist_id, seeds, warmup_iters, measure_iters, batch_size, concurrency, max_input_tokens, max_output_tokens
  - scheduler knobs: batching_window_ms, prefill_decode_interleave, queue_depth_limits, backpressure_mode
  - timestamps: started_at, finished_at, duration_s
- Artifact naming + uploader
  - Results directory is packed into a single tar.zst with a deterministic name: {suite}-{model_id}-{gpu}-{mode}-{commit_sha}-{timestamp}.tar.zst
  - Uploader writes a companion “index.jsonl” entry with the key metadata fields for quick querying in downstream aggregation.
  - Supports GCS and “drive mirror” via the existing internal artifact API (same endpoint the perf suite uses). Defaults to dry-run locally.
- Safety / privacy
  - We explicitly strip env vars and flags that match token/secret patterns.
  - Hostnames/GPU UUIDs are hashed (stable per run, not reversible) to preserve debuggability without leaking fleet details.
- Backwards compatibility
  - If metadata collection fails, the harness will still produce benchmark numbers, but CI and the matrix runner can optionally enforce `--require-metadata` (added here, default off).

Why this approach:
- Needed for reproducibility: reviewers can re-run a case and confirm it’s the same driver/CUDA and the same clocking regime.
- Needed for anomaly triage: we can quickly spot that a subset of runs used a different container digest or ran on a MIG-partitioned node.

Example output (abridged): {"schema_version":"1","git_commit_sha":"7f9a1d3e0c...","cuda_runtime_version":"12.4","nvidia_driver_version":"550.54.14","gpu_name":"NVIDIA H100 SXM","graphics_clock_mhz":"1710","power_limit_w":"700","model_id":"llama-3-70b-instruct","model_hash":"b6b2...","quant_mode":"fp8","suite_name":"top-hosted-models-benchmark-suite-v3","workload_id":"prefill_decode_mix_p50","batch_size":"8","concurrency":"32","started_at":"2026-02-15T03:22:11Z"}

Testing:
- Unit: metadata serialization + redaction rules
- Integration: harness emits metadata + uploader produces bundle + dry-run upload
- Manual: ran a small H100 microbench job and verified clocks/driver/container digest match nvidia-smi and container label

Follow-ups:
- Wire `--require-metadata` into benchmark-lab matrix runner defaults after we’ve validated on A100/H100 clusters.
- Add a tiny “metadata diff” helper for triage (compare two runs and highlight what changed).
commits: bench: write benchmark_metadata.json sidecar for microbench and e2e runs
bench: add artifact bundler + uploader with deterministic naming
bench: implement redaction + stable hashing for sensitive fields
tests: metadata schema validation + uploader dry-run coverage
docs: update harness README with artifact layout and flags
conversation:
Claire Dubois (review): Can we guarantee the manifest includes enough to explain the variance thread (driver/CUDA mismatch + clock drift)? Also please make schema version explicit.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added schema_version="1" and explicit nvidia_driver_version + cuda_runtime_version + container digest. Also added power_limit_w + mem_clock_mhz fields when available.

Noah Patel (review): Please ensure we don’t leak fleet internals (hostnames, UUIDs). Also: is model_hash stable across sharded checkpoints?
Rina Kobayashi (author): Hostname + GPU UUID now hashed with a per-run salt (stored in manifest) so it’s stable within a bundle but not reversible. For model_hash we hash the weights manifest/index file (covers shard list + sizes) rather than individual shard bytes.

Irene Choi (review): Uploader should never default to writing into prod buckets from a laptop. Also add MIG indicator; we’ve been bitten.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Default is `--dry-run`; actual upload requires `--upload` plus an explicit destination. Added mig_mode and partition size (when nvidia-smi reports it).

Isabella Rossi (review): Artifact naming needs to include kernel mode and scheduler config; otherwise microbench vs e2e gets confusing in Drive.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Name now includes `{mode}` and `workload_id`. Scheduler knobs are in metadata and also included in the index.jsonl row for aggregation.

Final approvals:
- Claire Dubois: Approved after schema/version updates
- Noah Patel: Approved after redaction/hashing changes
- Irene Choi: Approved after safe defaults
- Isabella Rossi: Approved
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Connor O'Brien. Squash commit: 6c2a0d1b0e (bench: artifact metadata + uploader).
release_notes: Benchmark harness now emits benchmark_metadata.json (schema v1) and can bundle/upload artifacts with deterministic naming. Enables reproducible comparisons across driver/CUDA/container/clocks/model revisions. No runtime serving behavior changes.
